entity_relationships.base: perform contract or customer-directed work on
entity_relationships.third_person: performs contract or customer-directed work on
entity_relationships.gerund: performing contract or customer-directed work on

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it, without tripping any of the guards below:

rules.text: The record says something substantive about the candidate {{entity_noun}} — describing an activity, arrangement, or dealing that involves it — rather than only naming it, listing it, or mentioning it in passing. Which party is involved is not this condition's subject; [SCR-2] and [SCR-3] decides that.

The candidate {{entity_noun}} is worked on to another party's order: items in it belong to, are specified by, or are branded for a customer, client, OEM, or brand owner — produced, machined, assembled, formulated, finished, packaged, or otherwise made to their specification, design, drawing, formula, or brand.

children.text: Selling them is NOT required. In contract work the customer owns and sells them, so the absence of any sale by the manufacturer is not a reason to fail.

rules.text: It is the manufacturer itself that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the candidate {{entity_noun}} — not a customer, supplier, distributor, or other third party that the manufacturer merely relates to.

children.text: Records refer to the manufacturer in question only as "the manufacturer" or "[the manufacturer]", never by name; other companies may appear by name or by their standing. A brand, trade name, former name, division, plant, or business unit of the manufacturer IS the manufacturer itself. A statement about the manufacturer's parent company or a sister brand counts as one about the manufacturer itself, and does not fail this condition merely for being attributed to them — unless the record shows the activity belongs to that company alone and not to the manufacturer.

A verb that leaves the commercial arrangement unstated does not by itself show whether the manufacturer is the party that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} it. Where the record says only that the manufacturer deals in the thing, without fixing in what capacity, the arrangement has not been established.
The manufacturer must be the shop doing the work, not the party sending it out. A record showing that someone else performs the contract work on items in the {{entity_noun}} fails this condition.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate has no bearing on the record's other candidates:

rules.text: The manufacturer's contract or customer-directed work on the candidate {{entity_noun}} is only aspirational, hoped-for, planned, or discontinued, rather than current and actual.
